body.x: Neuromeka (CEO Jonghoon Park) participated from January 6 to 9 (local time) in the HUMANOID M.AX Alliance pavilion at CES 2026 in Las Vegas, the United States.

Neuromeka is a robotics automation company that develops the full spectrum of technologies in-house, from core robot components and control software to AI-based applications. With full-stack capabilities spanning collaborative robots, industrial robots, autonomous mobile robots, and humanoid robot platforms, the company says it leads automation across the manufacturing, logistics, and service industries.

Neuromeka emphasized that it internalizes smart actuators for robot drive systems, high-performance motion controllers, and integrated control platforms through proprietary technologies, which reduces external dependence while securing both high quality and price competitiveness. Key technologies such as sensorless collision detection, AI-based imitation learning, and real-time control enable humans and robots to collaborate safely in shared spaces.

Beyond supplying individual products, Neuromeka is advancing into a next-generation robot platform company that combines robot foundation models (RFM) with AI control technologies, aiming to set new standards in industrial automation.

Neuromeka has continued to generate meaningful results, expanding applications of its collaborative robot “Indy” and “OPTi” series across major manufacturing sectors, including automotive, electronics, steel, and shipbuilding. In particular, through robot automation solutions specialized for shipyard welding processes, the company has demonstrated the feasibility of robotic deployment in high-difficulty, high-risk environments, proving its competitiveness in large-structure welding and repetitive welding automation. These efforts have received strong evaluations for improving productivity and enhancing worker safety in shipbuilding sites.

At the same time, Neuromeka has expanded its joint projects with large enterprises as well as mid-sized and small manufacturers, based on a diverse lineup that includes collaborative robots, high-payload robots, and dual-arm robots. Through integrated automation capabilities, including robot controllers and software, the company has gained hands-on experience in real-world mass-production processes.

body.cap: Neuromeka’s humanoid robot “EIR” is demonstrating the task of picking up and moving a sponge and plushies. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: At CES 2026, Neuromeka introduced its next-generation robot vision to the global market, focusing on the humanoid robot platform “EIR,” built on the industrial and collaborative robot technologies it has accumulated over the years.

Through EIR, Neuromeka showcased core technologies such as robot actuators, motion control, and integrated control software, while highlighting how control expertise and know-how gained from industrial sites, including shipyard welding robots, can extend to humanoid robots. This approach illustrated technological continuity between industrial robots and humanoid platforms.

EIR is a next-generation humanoid platform developed on the foundation of control and drive technologies proven in industrial and collaborative robots. Neuromeka designed and developed key components in-house, including robot actuators, motion control, and integrated control software, forming a full-stack architecture that meets the precision control and stability requirements of humanoid robots.

Neuromeka identified the direct application of control technologies validated in industrial environments as EIR’s greatest strength. Based on high-torque, high-precision actuators and real-time control technologies, the company secured repeatability, scalability, and system reliability, drawing on experience accumulated in demanding environments such as shipyard welding.

EIR also adopts an open platform architecture that supports expansion into diverse application fields beyond research and development. Through this approach, Neuromeka aims to evolve humanoid robots from one-off demonstration models into practical platforms that can scale across industrial and service domains.

body.x: Neuromeka continues to push global expansion, focusing on collaborative robots and automation solutions, and has exported to major markets including the United States, China, Germany, Australia, Brazil, and India since 2024. The company operates local subsidiaries in the United States and China and, on this basis, has installed frying automation templates and provided technical support for Kyochon Chicken's offline stores in Los Angeles and Shanghai. The solution enables expansion into other overseas Kyochon locations, creating opportunities for broader deployment within countries and for further exports to additional markets.

By country, Neuromeka has exported collaborative robots for medical endoscope manipulation to India, delivered welding automation solutions to Germany, and supplied F&B automation solutions to Australia and Brazil. Leveraging precision-control-based welding technologies as a core strength, the company is expanding its presence in the global welding automation market and plans to aggressively target the global machine tending market through collaboration with DN Solutions.

Looking ahead, Neuromeka aims to secure distribution partners in 20 countries by 2026 and to strengthen sales and technical support structures by identifying partners centered on welding and machine tending. On the product side, the company plans to expand exports of robot platforms, led by the flagship Indy series and the welding-specialized OPTi series, while also exporting robot components, such as reducers, motors, and actuators, based on its internally developed technologies. Neuromeka also plans to apply template-based solutions in education, welding, machine tending, and F&B, customized to meet local market needs.

In addition, Neuromeka intends to continue expanding exports by enhancing brand awareness and directly engaging buyers through participation in major global exhibitions such as CES, Automate, and Fabtech.

The HUMANOID M.AX Alliance is a public-private consultative body formed in April 2025 with the participation of 260 organizations and companies, including AI research institutes, robot manufacturers, component suppliers, and universities and research institutions. The alliance jointly promotes the demonstration and commercialization of AI-based humanoids in industrial environments. At CES 2026, the HUMANOID M.AX Alliance Pavilion went beyond simple product displays and presented a practical model for ecosystem building by connecting AI, platform, and component technologies.
